COP rose 0.65% today to $150.03, a modest gain that fits into a broader 5.86% climb over two weeks as oil prices remain elevated. US crude is trading at $103.37 per barrel, well above historical averages, while geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—including Iranian mine claims near the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attack concerns—keep supply risks front and center. These tensions have supported energy sector strength, though today's modest move suggests the market is taking a cautious wait-and-see approach ahead of Big Oil earnings reports.

The recent flip-flop in headlines matters: oil prices dipped Thursday on renewed U.S.-Iran peace talk prospects, but then Friday brought new reports of military reshuffles under the Trump administration and escalating Hormuz security fears, which could reignite supply concerns. For an integrated oil major like ConocoPhillips, both the high price environment and the geopolitical uncertainty create a mixed backdrop—higher oil prices are good for profits, but persistent war risk and policy shifts make the outlook harder to predict, which may explain why the stock is climbing but cautiously.
